# v2.72-dev — update progress works again, and the installer finishes the job

Three fixes to the non-root migration introduced in v2.70, all found by running it on a real Debian LXC rather than trusting that it worked.

> ### If you are stuck part-way through the v2.70 migration
>
> Run this on the server, **as root** (on an LXC you already are; on a VM prefix it with `sudo`):
>
> ```bash
> systemctl restart training-tracker
> ```
>
> That alone unblocks the "Update now" button. Updating to this release makes it unnecessary in future.

## Fixed

**The installer now restarts the app.** It used to *start* it, which does nothing when the app is already running — so the one command the v2.70 notes told you to run appeared to succeed while the app quietly carried on as root, and the update button kept refusing. The installer now restarts, and prints the account the app is actually running under so you can see it worked.

**Update progress no longer freezes at "Starting update…".** On some systems — including a standard unprivileged LXC — the update ran to completion but the progress bar never moved and the update log stayed empty. Everything the updater tried to record was being silently discarded. Progress and logs now work on every system.

**The same fault would have broken rollback.** If an update had failed and needed to roll back, the restore step would itself have failed, on the same systems, for the same reason. That is the worst possible moment to discover a bug, and it is now fixed along with everything else.

**Errors say what is wrong.** "Server returned an error" has been replaced with the actual reason, including the exact command to run when there is one. Failures that used to be discarded are now recorded in the system log where support can find them.

**Instructions no longer assume `sudo` is installed.** Several commands in the documentation and in the app were written as `sudo …`. Minimal LXC containers frequently do not have `sudo` at all — the whole reason this project avoids depending on it — so those instructions could not be followed on exactly the systems they were aimed at. They now show the plain command to run as root, noting `sudo` only where it applies.

## Notes

- The update progress file, update log, and `.env` change ownership slightly as part of this fix. This happens automatically; there is nothing to do.
